title: Flow-Fence Rate Controller and Progressive Degradation for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience tail amplification when multiple mid-priority services burst concurrently. Current admission logic uses coarse token buckets and preemptive shedding which can either underutilize headroom or drop critical requests abruptly. Goal: implement a 'flow-fence' rate controller that establishes soft per-flow and per-viewport fences, dynamically adjusts token reservation based on short-term SLO signals, and orchestrates progressive degradation across routing tiers (host, pool, region) to preserve critical throughput guarantees while minimizing user-facing errors. 

Scope: controller implemented in the dedicated routing plane that enforces: (1) per-customer and per-route soft fences, (2) burst slots that are time-limited and borrowed from a shared headroom pool, (3) latency-aware priority queuing with bounded queuing time, and (4) staged degradation policies that demote or degrade non-critical features before shedding guaranteed-throughput traffic. Not in scope: storage-layer QoS changes, long-term pricing changes, or private deployment packaging (handled in follow-ups).

Technical approach: 
- Admission model: replace single global token bucket with a hierarchy: global headroom -> regional fence -> pool fence -> route fence. Fences are soft: they permit slight oversubscription for short windows but expose consumption signals to the autoscaler.
- Token accounting: implement per-fence token accounting with leaky-bucket recharge and a borrowable burst reservoir. Reservoir borrow is tracked with exponential backoff to avoid repeated bursts.
- Latency SLO feedback: integrate short-window p99 latency and queue length signals. If tail latency crosses thresholds, the controller tightens fences and initiates progressive degradation (step-downs) instead of immediate wholesale shedding.
- Progressive degradation: ordered feature demotion plan per customer (eg. disable large-context caching, reduce sampling temperature, switch to lower-quantized model variant, reduce max_tokens). Degradation rules are expressed as a prioritized list and evaluated atomically.
- Queueing & deadline enforcement: implement bounded in-memory queues per-route with deadline-aware dequeue. Requests that exceed queue deadline are either fast-failed with structured error and suggested retry-after, or routed to fallback model variants if configured.
- Observability: emit fine-grained metrics (fence_consumption, headroom_borrow_rate, progressive_degrades, queue_deadlines_missed) and traces that correlate request -> fence decisions.

Acceptance criteria: 
- New controller deployed behind feature flag for a single Canary dedicated pool with synthetic workload. 
- Under controlled burst test, tail p99 latency remains within 1.2x baseline while critical-route throughput meets reserved guarantee for 95% of test windows. 
- Headroom borrowing is rate-limited and visible via dashboard metrics; borrow rate must drop to zero within configured cooldown windows. 
- Progressive degradation executes the configured demotion sequence and logs a structured event per request. 
- New metrics and dashboards are available in Console and alert if queue_deadlines_missed > 1% over 5m windows.

Implementation milestones: 
1) Design doc + API contract for fences and degradation rules (owner: Aisha) (ETA 2026-03-05). 
2) Local runtime implementation of hierarchical fences and token accounting (owner: Marco) (ETA 2026-03-12). 
3) Integrate latency SLO signals and degradation executor (owner: Marco) (ETA 2026-03-15). 
4) Canary rollout + synthetic test harness + dashboards (owner: SRE) (ETA 2026-03-19). 
5) Post-canary tuning and wider rollout (ETA 2026-03-29).

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Soft fences vs hard quotas: soft fences allow temporary oversubscription for improved utilization but require careful cooldown logic to avoid cascading borrow. We prioritize availability of guaranteed routes over absolute enforcement.
- Progressive degradation complexity: adds per-customer rule management; mitigated by shipping gated config schema and sane defaults.
- Queueing memory vs headroom cost: bounded queues reduce latency tail amplification but consume memory per route; we limit queue depth and prefer early fast-fail for low-priority traffic.

Testing plan: 
- Unit tests for token accounting and borrow/cooldown semantics. 
- Integration tests with autoscaler simulator to ensure borrow signals trigger scale-ups only when appropriate. 
- Synthetic load tests with mixed priority workload and failure injection to validate progressive-degrade ordering.

Rollout & feature flagging: 
- Feature flag group: routing.flow_fence_v1 with targetable rollout (canary pool id). 
- Metrics gated: only enable in pools with observability hooks; fail closed on missing telemetry. 

Monitoring & alerts: 
- Console dashboard: fence_utilization (per-fence), headroom_borrow_rate, progressive_degrades, queue_deadline_misses, guarantee_violation_rate. 
- Alerts: p99_latency_increase > 1.5x baseline OR guarantee_violation_rate > 0.5% for > 5m -> pager for oncall. 

Next steps: finalize API contract, land proto changes for fence telemetry, and schedule canary with SRE.
acceptance_criteria: Feature available behind routing.flow_fence_v1 feature flag and enabled for a canary dedicated pool
Under synthetic burst tests, p99 latency <= 1.2x baseline while critical-route throughput >= reserved guarantee for 95% of windows
Headroom borrow rate metric visible and returns to zero within configured cooldown time during tests
Progressive degradation executes configured demotion rules and emits structured events
Dashboards and alerts for queue_deadlines_missed and guarantee_violation_rate exist in Console

risk_mitigation: Gate behind feature flag and only run in pools with full telemetry. Add emergency kill switch to immediately disable soft borrow and force strict quotas. Maintain a canary-only rollout until two weeks of stable metrics. Document demotion sequences and provide opt-out per-customer via console.
rollout_plan: Canary in single dedicated pool -> expand to 10% of pools after 72h stable metrics -> 50% after 1 week -> global rollout. Each stage has automated rollback on guarantee_violation_rate or p99 spikes. Coordinate with SRE for scaling tests.
